 Sam Merrill 
 CLE 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Sam Merrill (elbow) is out for Monday’s game against the Bulls. 
 Merrill will miss a sixth straight game on Monday as he continues to deal with a right elbow injury. His absence has freed up additional minutes for Meleek Thomas, who’s made the most of his opportunities. 
 Tyrese Proctor 
 CLE 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Tyrese Proctor recorded a triple-double with a team-high 24 points (10-of-19 FGs), 11 rebounds and 10 assists to lead the Cavaliers to a 127-117 win over the Mavericks on Saturday. 
 The Cavaliers were without their entire starting five on the second night of a back-to-back, with nationwide travel disruptions on Friday contributing to a lengthy list of absences. Donovan Mitchell (knee), James Harden (calf), Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jarrett Allen (knee) were all ruled out, while Evan Mobley missed his second consecutive game due to a toe sprain he sustained earlier this week. Proctor stepped up to lead Cleveland to an unexpected win by shooting over 50 percent from the floor, including 4-of-13 from three-point range. It was his first career triple-double. He’s played over 22 minutes in five consecutive games and has topped 15 points in three straight during that span. Cleveland has a three-game week coming up with home matchups against the Bulls, Grizzlies and Pacers. 
 Meleek Thomas 
 CLE 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Meleek Thomas, Tyrese Proctor, Jaylon Tyson, Mario Hezonja and Thomas Bryant will start against the Mavericks on Saturday. 
 The Cavs played in Miami on Friday and then had flight delays (like everyone did) that prevented them from returning to Cleveland when they intended. So they’re resting the entire starting five. It will be five new starters for the Cavs, though they will all likely return to reserve roles in their next game.

 #45 
 Donovan Mitchell (knee) has been ruled out against the Mavericks on Saturday. 
 Mitchell will be unavailable, as will the other four typical starters for Cleveland. Rookie Meleek Thomas should get the starting nod in place of Mitchell. Thomas has been excellent this season, and this should be a good opportunity for him.
